div.div: Who is speaking: the face's moving mouth SELECTS, the coarse microphone bearing only gates and corroborates, and when the voice has no face the label is 'unidentified', because a confident wrong name costs more than no name
A. TOP-DOWN SCENE AT THE STAND (positions are a drawing choice, not data)
head-camera field of view 90 deg [I11]
amber dashed = face window +-40 deg [I10] = gate 15 deg [I9] + half a bin [calc]
grey dashed = on-chip direction bins, 45 deg each (8 directions) [I8]

visitor_1
mouth moving

visitor_2
silent

bystander, outside
the window, silent

a phone playing
speech, OFF camera

ROBOT
mic array
visitor_1 and visitor_2 share ONE bin and both sit inside the window: the bearing ABSTAINS and defers to active-speaker detection, which picks visitor_1 by the moving mouth.

The phone's bearing has NO face: positive evidence for 'unidentified'. It must not be pinned on the silent person in front. While the robot itself speaks, and for 400 ms after [I12], DoA evidence is ignored (the loudest direction may be the robot).

WHY A SMALL ARRAY IS COARSE (public physics)
sound 343 m/s [P1] -> largest delay across a 10 cm pair 292 us [P2]
one sample at 16 kHz = 62.5 us [P3] = 2.1 cm of path [P4] -> an integer lag resolves only about 12.4 deg near broadside [P5]
phase wraps above c / 2d: 3.4 kHz for a 5 cm pair [P6], 1.7 kHz for 10 cm [P7] (spatial aliasing)
So estimators interpolate below one sample (GCC-PHAT, SRP-PHAT), and small chips often report only a bin.

FUSION RULE (an invariant, not a tuning default): ASD selects among visible faces; DoA gates, breaks ties and corroborates; the loudest direction never selects on its own. DoA binds to a visual track, never stands alone.
TIERED LABELS after speech start (to scale): attach now, refine, repair before the NEXT turn
T0 250 ms [I13]: DoA x visible faces; never blocks a response
T1 by 1 s [I14]: ASD picks the talker; re-evaluated every frame
T2 up to 4 s [I15]: voice and face embeddings confirm or repair
0 s
1 s
2 s
3 s
4 s
ATTRIBUTION LADDER, per turn (first rung that succeeds wins)
1 ASD among faces big enough to score (at least 40 px wide [I19])
2 voice match: turn of 1.2 s or more [I16], cosine 0.55 [I17] and margin 0.15 [I18]; the only path that can name an off-camera voice
3 ABSTAIN: visitor_id null + a reason (off camera, contradicted, too short, blend). No sentinel id.

'SHOULD I RESPOND?' is about DIRECTEDNESS: under doubt, lean toward answering. An over-response is recoverable ('oh, were you asking me?'); silence toward an engaged visitor is not. Directedness ('someone off camera is addressing you') ships in the same change as abstention.

'WHO SAID IT?' is about IDENTITY: be strict. A churning id stream cost 30% more input tokens per response [I20], and one wrong bind passed to the next 4 turns [I21] through a 'last active speaker' fallback. A missing label is far cheaper than a wrong one.

Legend: circles = people or sound sources (green = talking, blue = silent visitor, grey = bystander, red = off-camera source) | green lines = camera field of view | amber dashed = face-matching window | grey dashed = direction bins.

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown. [Pn] = public (a paper, standard or physics value, or my arithmetic on one); [In] = illustrative (a round design value of the right order; never a measurement of a real robot or visitor); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B2-who-is-speaking.md (DoA basics, the fusion rule, tiered labels, the robot's own voice, honest abstention, voices banked carefully, passing attribution to the model; 'check the input-size gate'). [calc]: window = 15 + 45 / 2, rounded to 40 deg; checked 0.10 m / 343 m/s = 292 us and asin(343 m/s x 62.5 us / 10 cm) = 12.4 deg.
[P1] speed_of_sound_20c = 343 m/s. public: dry air at 20 degrees C (standard physics value)
[P2] tdoa_max_10cm = 292 us. public: my arithmetic: 0.10 m / speed_of_sound_20c, the largest delay between two microphones 10 cm apart (sound arriving along the axis)
[P3] sample_period_16k = 62.5 us. public: my arithmetic: 1 / 16 000 Hz
[P4] sample_path_16k = 2.1 cm of path difference per sample. public: my arithmetic: speed_of_sound_20c x sample_period_16k
[P5] one_sample_angle_10cm_16k = 12.4 degrees near broadside. public: my arithmetic: asin(sample_path_16k / 10 cm); why integer-lag cross-correlation is coarse and sub-sample interpolation (GCC-PHAT peak interpolation) is used
[P6] spatial_alias_5cm = 3.4 kHz. public: my arithmetic: f < c / (2 d) with d = 5 cm; above this a pair's phase difference wraps (spatial aliasing)
[P7] spatial_alias_10cm = 1.7 kHz. public: my arithmetic: f < c / (2 d) with d = 10 cm
[I8] doa_bin_illustrative = 45 degrees per direction bin (8 bins). illustrative coarse on-chip direction-of-arrival quantisation
[I9] doa_face_gate_illustrative = 15 degrees (nominal gate between a bearing and a face). illustrative
[I10] doa_effective_window_illustrative = 40 degrees either side (gate widened by bin uncertainty). illustrative: my arithmetic, rounded: doa_face_gate_illustrative + half of doa_bin_illustrative
[I11] fov_true_illustrative = 90 degrees. illustrative true horizontal field of view of the head camera
[I12] self_speech_tail_illustrative = 400 ms. illustrative suppression tail after the robot stops speaking (reverberation decay + label latency)
[I13] label_t0_illustrative = 250 ms after speech start. illustrative first provisional speaker label
[I14] label_t1_illustrative = 1 s. illustrative mouth-motion refinement
[I15] label_t2_illustrative = 4 s (latest). illustrative voice-identity confirmation at or after end of turn
[I16] voice_embedding_min_illustrative = 1.2 s. illustrative minimum speech for a usable voice embedding; public speaker-verification work reports degradation for utterances of a few seconds or less
[I17] voice_match_cosine_illustrative = 0.55 cosine similarity. illustrative match gate
[I18] voice_match_margin_illustrative = 0.15 cosine (top-1 minus top-2). illustrative margin gate
[I19] asd_min_face_illustrative = 40 px face width. illustrative input-size gate of an active-speaker detector
[I20] id_churn_token_cost_illustrative = 0.3 fractional increase in input tokens per response. illustrative cost of a churning speaker-id stream to a speech-to-speech model
[I21] cascade_turns_illustrative = 4 turns. illustrative number of later turns that inherit one wrong bind through a 'last active speaker' fallback
